description: We are NovaAI, a team of AI engineers, developers, and creators based in Mansoura. We are built to tackle advanced space and earth challenges using AI and software solutions. Ready for the next frontier!
summary:
For the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, we developed NOVA, an interactive 3D storytelling experience that brings discarded space hardware back to life. Our project specifically focuses on the Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage and the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package (EASEP).

To address the challenge, we transformed dry technical archives from the NSSDCA into a playable, emotional journey. Players explore a cinematic lunar landscape, locate the dormant EASEP, and solve puzzles to restore its power. Once revived, the hardware "speaks" through an interactive narrative game. Based on actual NASA telemetry and mission logs, players can uncover the equipment's historic discoveries, the lunar quakes it measured, and the extreme temperatures it endured before its final transmission.

NOVA is important because it bridges the gap between raw scientific data and human empathy. Instead of reading static datasets, young learners emotionally connect with space history, ensuring the scientific legacy of these silent machines inspires future generations.
details:
What it does and how it works

We built NOVA as an interactive 3D storytelling experience to bring forgotten space hardware back to life. When you play it, you step into a lunar environment and head straight to the exact landing coordinates of the Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage and the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package (EASEP). To move forward, you have to interact with the environment, clear away decades of moon dust, and solve a short puzzle to temporarily restore power to the EASEP's solar panels. Once it wakes up, a narrative interface opens up. This lets players dive into the machine's actual historical logs, learn about the lunar quakes it recorded, and see the extreme temperatures it survived right up until its final transmission on August 27, 1969.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The main goal of NOVA is to take really dense, technical NASA data and turn it into something accessible and emotional. Instead of just reading dry textbooks or looking at spreadsheets, people actually get to experience the data. We want to bridge the gap between hard scientific history and human empathy. By giving a voice to these silent machines that paved the way for modern space exploration, we're hoping to inspire the Artemis generation and build a deeper appreciation for the early space missions.

Tools, Hardware, and Software Used

We used a mix of creative and technical tools to put this together:

  • Unreal Engine 5.8.4: This was our core engine for building the 3D lunar environment, setting up the lighting, and programming the interactions.
  • Blender 5.0: We used this to 3D model the Apollo 11 Descent Stage and EASEP equipment as accurately as possible.
  • Substance 3D Painter: This helped us apply realistic, weathered textures so the equipment actually looked like it had been sitting in lunar dust and radiation for decades.
  • Photoshop 2025: Used for our concept art, UI design, and getting that retro VHS-style branding right.
  • CapCut: For editing the final demo video.
  • ElevenLabs: We used this to generate the voiceover narration for our pitch.
  • Suno: To create the ambient, melancholic space soundtrack in the background.

How Our Project is Creative

We wanted to approach the data differently by treating the space hardware almost like a character. Instead of just making a standard data dashboard or a basic 3D viewer, we gave the EASEP a story to tell. We also went heavy on a retro-futuristic vibe, using vintage CRT and VHS glitch effects to really capture that 1960s Apollo era feel. It is a mix of nostalgic art direction and modern interactive storytelling.

Factors Our Team Considered

  • Scientific Accuracy: It was really important to us that the coordinates (0.67416 N, 23.47314 E), equipment specs, and mission timelines were strictly based on the real NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA).
  • Emotional Resonance: We spent a lot of time tweaking the atmosphere, lighting, and sound design to make sure players actually feel the "magnificent desolation" of the Moon.
  • Accessibility: We kept the interactions simple and intuitive. We wanted users of all ages and backgrounds to be able to jump in and learn something without needing to be gamers or space experts.
